statements.proposition: The change keeps isURL behaviour for legitimate URLs unchanged (no regression for valid URLs).
statements.label: FALSE
statements.note: Concrete regression: scheme-less host:port URLs that validated at base are rejected at head, because the new regex treats 'example.com' as a scheme and returns false (not in protocols list / no '//').
evidence: Built base 6f436be and head ec9c86f, ran isURL with default options: base isURL('example.com:8080')=true, isURL('www.example.com:80/path')=true, isURL('sub.example.com:443?x=1')=true; head returns false for all three
Head also false for 'localhost:3000' with require_tld:false (base true); both are legitimate host:port URLs
Existing 298 mocha tests do not cover this, so the PR's own suite does not catch it
